view: Today's -14.3% gap-to-low on the CEO resignation followed by a +10.4% recovery on 3.8x volume is the capitulation shape I said was missing, but the bar is still open and the trigger is a governance shock, not a sentiment washout, so it is a candidate climax and not a confirmed bottom. Sentiment now tilts down-skewed over 2 weeks (testimony before Thanksgiving, earnings 11-17 under an interim CEO); tactical stance Wait, and the chair should rule on TB2 first because it would pause all buying regardless of what sentiment says.

Owner-bias audit for a day like this: (1) Confirmation bias - I named this reversal shape as what capitulation needs, and now it appears; the owner (and I) will want to call the bottom. It is an open bar on a single-name shock: wait for the close and Friday's weekly bar. (2) FOMO / urgency - a +10.4% rip off the low creates fear of missing the bottom; the rule-based answer is that a TB2 review comes before any buy, and missing the exact low costs less than buying into an unresolved governance event. (3) Anchoring - on today's low 148.80 as 'the bottom', on the ATH 243.37 as 'fair value', and on Huang's era as the base case; the company's leadership changed, so old anchors carry less information. (4) Rationalising the rule away - the thesis breaks were written calmly precisely so they would bind on a day like today (Kahneman: System 2 pre-commitment beats System 1 in the moment); if the owner wants to argue 'not under legal pressure', write the reason down and have the red team challenge it before acting. (5) Lessons log: weekly RSI 32.9 is on an open bar and above 30 - still not oversold.
Stance (sentiment lane only): tactical Wait; strategic stance deferred to the chair's TB2 ruling. Never place or suggest orders; ladder changes need owner approval.

Cross-domain: VIX 17.62 and indices higher while NVDA gapped -13.1% means the market is pricing an idiosyncratic risk; relative-strength and narrative members should test whether SOX/peers held up (sector contagion vs single-name).

Pre-mortem: three months on, this was badly wrong most likely because today was the climax low (the n=4 '2w drop <=-15%' base rate was right) and the governance shock was resolved quickly, so my down skew left the owner waiting while price recovered.
